anomalies.observed: In the POWER TRAIN sheet the TPS62933 buck feedback divider is drawn as R48 = 523 kΩ from the +5V output node down to the FB pin, with R50 = 10 kΩ from FB to GND (division ratio ≈ 53.3 : 1).
anomalies.expected: The TPS62933 regulates its FB pin to 0.8 V (the sheet even labels the FB net "/0V8_BK"), so for the specified 5 V output the divider must be ≈ 5.25 : 1 — the datasheet value is a 52.3 kΩ top resistor with a 10 kΩ bottom resistor. 523 kΩ with 10 kΩ calls for 0.8 × (1 + 523/10) ≈ 42.6 V, which the 24 V input can never reach.

evidence.quote: U1 — TPS62933 (TI) | 24 V → 5 V synchronous buck regulator, 3 A
feedback via R13/R14/R15, BST cap C12, soft-start cap C10, as named by the /BST_BK, /RT_BK, /SS_BK, /0V8_BK nets
POWER TRAIN sheet: "R48 523k" from the +5V node to the FB-divider node and "R50 10k" from that node to GND, fed to U4 (TPS62933) FB pin

anomalies.impact: The converter would never reach regulation: it would run at maximum duty cycle and the "+5V" rail would sit close to the 24 V input, over-volting the AZ1117 3.3 V LDO, the ESP32-C6-DevKit and all other 5 V/3.3 V circuitry on the board.

parsed.summary: The design is largely as specified, but the TPS62933 24 V→5 V buck feedback divider in the POWER TRAIN sheet is wrong by a factor of ten (R48 = 523 kΩ with R50 = 10 kΩ), which programs ≈42 V instead of 5 V and would destroy the downstream 5 V/3.3 V rails and MCU.
